text.p: Bonds closed down, dragged lower by the fall of Treasuries on the back of strong growth in U.S. jobs and the NAPM prices index which pointed to possible inflationary tension, traders said.
The opening on Monday will be determined by how Treasuries finish on Friday, traders said.
Despite the weakness, the Portuguese market outperformed the Bunds and the Spanish Bonos, tightening the spreads with both.
"The numbers in the United States awakened expectations of a rate rise and the Treasuries fell heavily. Europe could not escape the fall," said one trader.
"The problem is to know whether there is going to be any recovery in foreign markets on Monday," added another.
With virtually no interest in the shorter end, the spread narrowed slightly to 100 basis points.
